data.narrative:
OpenStar, a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Ratu Mataira and Thomas Berry, is evaluated against a fragmented comp universe of 11 peers (3 public, 8 private) spanning advanced reactor and SMR development. The peer set includes public companies OKLO, NNE, and SMR, alongside private firms including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

Given OpenStar's Seed stage and $35M total raised to date, a direct peer-median approach proved inapplicable. The Nuclear Energy subsector contains only one same-stage comparable and one adjacent-stage peer; narrower filtering yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to anchor a credible median. A broad all-sector median would obscure stage-specific and sector-specific risk factors. Consequently, the valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the $35M raised baseline, implying $88M post-money valuation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $74M to $101M, with a median of $88M. This range reflects reasonable variance around the single applicable method but underscores a material constraint: the narrow nuclear-energy peer set at Seed stage limits triangulation robustness. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed recent fundraising rounds among comparable-stage nuclear companies and whether OpenStar's technology pathway and capital intensity align with the broader cohort. Additional comps or disclosed transaction data would meaningfully narrow this range.
